title: Local photos are hidden when the server is unconfigured
current_state: At 01:24 and 01:25, dated timeline media tiles render as uniform gray placeholders while logged out or unconfigured. At 01:26, after server login, the corresponding dated positions render recognizable photos, strongly indicating the local assets were already available.
problem: This blocks the core task of browsing device photos and makes users infer that media is missing, corrupted, or still loading. Uniform placeholders do not distinguish loading, unavailable, and authentication-gated states.
recommendation: Keep local thumbnail retrieval independent from server authentication. Render device media whenever photo-library permission exists; use placeholders only for bounded loading, expose accessible error or unavailable states, and represent server status with a secondary badge or overlay.
notes: Visual evidence: screenshots 01.24.45, 01.25.02, and 01.26.44. Screen-reader behavior not yet verified.

title: Sticky source selector overlaps the iOS safe area
current_state: After scrolling in the 01:25 screenshot, the sticky Teléfono | Todo | Servidor selector moves underneath the iOS status bar; system indicators visibly overlap its labels and selected segment.
problem: The overlap degrades legibility and makes touch targets compete visually with system UI, increasing uncertain or missed taps.
recommendation: Anchor the sticky selector below the dynamic top safe-area inset, provide an opaque or blurred sticky background, preserve 44x44 pt touch targets, and verify notched and Dynamic Island devices, larger text, and VoiceOver focus order.
notes: Visual evidence: screenshot 01.25.02. Actual hit targets and VoiceOver order not yet verified.

title: Server availability is enforced above the capability boundary
current_state: The local-first shell lacks a consistent capability-scoped contract: route-level authentication guards can replace an entire mixed surface and hide locally available content when no authenticated server is available.
problem: Users cannot predict which features require the server and may interpret unavailable remote capabilities as missing local data.
recommendation: Classify each feature as local, mixed, or server-only. Preserve local content on mixed screens and apply a reusable ServerCapabilityNotice only at the dependent section boundary, with state-specific actions for unconfigured, offline, and reauthentication states.
notes: Applies to Search, Albums, Library, and People. Code mapping still required before implementation.
